title: Prefill early-exit transform: fingerprint-based bypass to avoid heavy kernel dispatch
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: A non-trivial fraction of prefill requests are small, ASCII-dominant prompts where the full tokenizer + unicode normalization + microkernel dispatch path is overkill. Each request currently pays a ~2.5-4ms fixed prefill-side overhead (normalize -> tokenize -> dispatch), which dominates end-to-end latency for short prompts. Goals: 1) Reduce fixed per-request prefill overhead for common, simple prompts. 2) Avoid kernel dispatch (and associated scheduling/queueing) when the request can be satisfied by a lightweight pass. 3) Maintain correctness for complex inputs (unicode, multipart, system tokens) and be safe under experiment rollouts.
approach: Implement an early-exit prefill transform that computes a compact fingerprint of the incoming prompt before running the full normalization/tokenization pipeline. The fingerprint has three inexpensive checks: (a) ASCII-only predicate, (b) token-separable-by-whitespace heuristic, and (c) prefix-length bound (e.g., <= 128 chars). If all checks pass, run a lightweight ASCII-normalizer + whitespace-split token mapper that produces tokens using a fallback micro-vocab mapping. If the lightweight mapper yields a stable token sequence that matches validation heuristics, skip the heavy tokenizer and prevent kernel endpoint dispatch for a single-token or small-token prefill. Otherwise fall back to the full pipeline.
design_details: Fingerprint step is pure CPU and must be branch-friendly and SIMD-friendly (vectorized ASCII scan + length checks). Aim for <200ns on our baselines. The lightweight mapper uses a precompiled ASCII token mapping table (compact trie) that maps whitespace-separated tokens into token ids for a conservative subset of the vocabulary (common words and punctuation). If a word is not in the table, mark as miss and fall back. Validation rules: total token count <= 32, no special/system tokens, no emoji/combining chars, and total encoded length < 256 bytes. Telemetry: emit a per-request tag: early_exit:{hit|miss}:{reason}. Configuration: feature flag per-tenant, rollout via Console with percentage and min-throughput constraints.
benchmarks: Baseline (full pipeline, short prompt ~12 chars): median prefill latency = 3.2ms. Early-exit path (ASCII simple prompts): median prefill latency = 0.9ms. End-to-end median latency reduction for 1-2 token prompts in hosted flow: ~1.5-2.3ms. Kernel dispatch avoided in ~18% of production prefill requests in the sample trace used. Reduced kernel queue length by ~11% during peak microbursts.
acceptance_criteria: Correctness: no decoding regressions observed on canonical prompt suite (run eval-suite/prefill-smoke — verify equivalence for early-exit candidates). Performance: early-exit path median prefill latency < 1.2ms and early-exit hit rate >= 10% in controlled rollout sample. Safety: telemetry shows <0.1% of early-exit hits that later require full re-dispatch. Observability: Console shows early_exit.* metrics + per-tenant rollout status.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary internal cluster with feature flag set to 5% traffic, enable detailed logging. Run for 48 hours. 2) Expand to 20% if no correctness/regression signals. Monitor kernel queue metrics and SLOs. 3) Target full rollout for hosted tier and opt-in for Dedicated in runtime-1.20.
risks_tradeoffs: Risk of subtle tokenization mismatch for edge unicode cases; mitigated by conservative mapping table and strict validation. Slightly increased CPU on front-end pod for fingerprinting; cost vs. saved kernel scheduling should be net positive for short prompt heavy tenants. Complexity of maintaining ASCII fallback vocab; will require a lightweight sync process with model vocab updates.
open_questions: What should the conservative subset size be? (initial: 24k high-frequency terms -> stored as compressed trie ~200KB). Should we persist micro-vocab per model family? How to expose metrics per-tenant without telemetry noise?
